guide.summary: Museums, the Jewish Quarter, Strahov, Vyšehrad and the zoo, with historic cafés, bakeries, Czech pubs, tasting menus and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Keep Mondays for the National Museum, Museum Kampa, the Mucha Museum or the zoo, because the Trade Fair Palace, the National Technical Museum and the Museum of Prague's main building close that day, and avoid Saturdays for the Jewish Museum.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The National Gallery's Trade Fair Palace, the National Technical Museum and the Museum of Prague's main building and House at the Golden Ring are closed on Mondays. The Jewish Museum in Prague closes on Saturdays and Jewish holidays.

toolkit.label: Autumn hours
toolkit.copy: From 18 October the Jewish Museum sites close at 4:30 p.m., and Prague Zoo closes at 5 pm in October and 4 pm in November, with ticket offices and pavilions closing earlier.

toolkit.label: Booking and walk-ins
toolkit.copy: Café Imperial suggests reserving "even weeks in advance", and Field holds reservations for only 15 minutes. Café Slavia says you rarely need to book, takes weekend reservations only from 19:00 and none on public holidays.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Field asks for smart casual and is not suitable for children under 6. At the Rudolfinum, the Czech Philharmonic turns no one away for clothing, though a dark suit or business formal is the safe choice for evening concerts.

guide.dek: Plan museum days around Monday and Saturday closures, book Café Imperial and Field ahead, and save one evening for a concert at the Rudolfinum or the Municipal House.
intro: This Prague guide is built from places whose own websites were read on 21 October 2026. You can start at the National Museum's Historical Building at Václavské náměstí 68, open daily from 10:00 to 18:00, where Maps and Atlases from the Kinsky Library runs until 3 January 2027. Entry pauses when the building is full, usually around weekend noon. The Jewish Museum in Prague, based at Maiselova 15, opens 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. from 18 October and closes on Saturdays and Jewish holidays. Up at Hradčany, the Strahov Monastery library and gallery open from 9:00 to 17:00.

For art, Museum Kampa in Malá Strana opens daily from 10 am to 6 pm and shows Milan Kunc – Pop Renaissance until 17 January 2027. The Mucha Museum on Panská opens daily from 10:00 to 18:00. The National Gallery's Trade Fair Palace in Prague 7 has Zbyněk Sekal — Blue Flower until 31 January 2027 but closes on Mondays. The Museum of Prague's House at the Golden Ring on Týnská covers Prague under Charles IV, and its main building on Na Poříčí stays open until 8 pm on Thursdays.

With children, you can try Prague Zoo in Troja, open 9 am to 5 pm in October and to 4 pm in November and December. The National Technical Museum on Kostelní opens Tuesday to Sunday and has The Saga of the Hainz Family from 14 October 2026. The Museum of Prague's free Cloud exhibition is aimed at young children. In the evening, the Czech Philharmonic plays the Rudolfinum with Semyon Bychkov on 22 and 23 October, and the Municipal House stages Rossini's Le Comte Ory on 24 October.

For food, Café Imperial on Na Poříčí serves a breakfast buffet from 7:00 daily and says it is in the Michelin Guide 2026. Eska bakes in Karlín and Letná, and Myšák on Vodičkova serves Czech desserts. For Czech beer, Lokál Dlouhááá opens from 11:00 and U Zlatého tygra on Husova from 15:00. Field and La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise take reservations, and Field holds a table for only 15 minutes. Afterwards, Hemingway Bar opens from 17:00 and Anonymous Bar on Michalská serves until 02:00.
summaryCards: Pair the National Museum on Wenceslas Square with a weekday at the Jewish Museum, which closes on Saturdays, then walk up to the Strahov Monastery library, open 9:00 to 17:00.
Start with the 7:00 breakfast buffet at Café Imperial or a pastry at Eska in Letná, then spend the late morning at Museum Kampa, open daily from 10 am.
Reserve Café Imperial and Field ahead, check concert dates for the Rudolfinum and the Municipal House, and remember several museums close on Mondays.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Prague Castle's official site (hrad.cz) refused automated reading with HTTP 403, so the castle is not included; that is not evidence of closure. Black Angel's Bar could not be read (connection reset), and U Fleků's contact page returned 404, so both are left out. Petřín Lookout Tower and the Old Town Bridge Tower are not listed on the Museum of Prague's own site, and tourism-board pages were excluded by method. Charles Bridge, Old Town Square and the Letná viewpoint are public spaces with no operator page giving operating evidence. Several places (Café Louvre, Café Savoy, Café Slavia, Kantýna, La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise, Field, Hemingway Bar, Můj šálek kávy, both Eska branches and the House at the Golden Ring) showed current hours or booking but no 2026-dated content, and the Mucha Museum, U Zlatého tygra and Anonymous Bar carried only a 2026 copyright line. Prague Zoo's monthly hours and news gave no year. Vyšehrad and the Strahov Monastery published only partial hours, and Municipal House tour hours and Rudolfinum box-office hours were not on the pages read.
